messages:
Alex G: Heads up — after yesterday's retention tweak the telemetry-exporter pods spiked CPU ~3x and p99 export latency jumped from 120ms -> 850ms. Noticed it during the tail-end of a big import. :eyes:
Maria L: Ugh. Which change exactly? The retention prune window or the Kafka batching change?
Jamal R: I deployed the retention policy change (reduce active window from 30d -> 14d) yesterday at 23:10. It also kicked off a backfill job to reindex/trim spans. Could that flurry be the cause?
Alex G: The CPU spike correlates with backfill start. But exporter CPU stayed high even after backfill completed. Means exporter is doing more work per-span somehow.
Maria L: Can you paste exporter config and recent profiler snippet?
Alex G: Sure — exporter config (from k8s configmap):
```yaml
otel:
  exporters:
    kafka:
      brokers: ["kafka-01:9092"]
      compression: none
  batching:
    max_export_batch_size: 1024
    schedule_delay_millis: 50
  processors:
    resource: {}
    memory_limiter:
      check_interval: 5s
      limit_mib: 2048
```
Infra-bot: deployment/telemetry-exporter/rollout started by Jamal R at 2026-03-17T23:09:12Z
Kevin P: profiler flame snippet from top process (shortened):
```
60%  exporter  exporter::serialize_spans
20%  exporter  exporter::kafka_send
8%   exporter  exporter::json_encode
```
Tia S: serialize_spans up to 60% is suspicious — are we deduping attributes or expanding attrs for retention logic?
Jamal R: Retention backfill runs a scan to mark old traces and adds a couple attributes (retained:false/true) for bookkeeping. That touches span attributes. Maybe we accidentally moved attribute mutation into hot path.
Maria L: Does OTLP pipeline do attribute copying per span? If we're cloning attr maps for every export that can blow CPU and allocs. Any allocation traces?
Alex G: Yes GC pressure visible — p99 GC pause increased during the spike. Allocation profile shows many small maps.
SRE Oncall: From the metrics side, export batch size stayed around 200-300 despite max 1024. schedule_delay is 50ms but backlog made exporter flush often. Could be suboptimal batching with our current queue size and concurrency settings.
Kevin P: Quick experiments I ran: increasing `schedule_delay_millis` to 200ms and bumping `max_export_batch_size` to 2048 brought CPU down ~30% and p99 latency to ~260ms in a dev replay. However this increases end-to-end export lag which may affect retention correctness.
Tia S: Other lever: enable compression on Kafka (lz4) to reduce network CPU, and avoid per-span JSON encode by switching to proto or efficient serializer. But proto change is a bigger rollout.
Maria L: For short-term: revert the backfill's attribute mutation to a separate post-process job (avoid touching live exporter path), and increase batch window temporarily.
Alex G: I'm going to patch config: set schedule_delay_millis=200, max_export_batch_size=2048, enable compression=lz4. Also add a quick env var to short-circuit attribute mutation in exporter. Will roll canary first.
Infra-bot: deployment/telemetry-exporter/rollout paused — canary metric p99=320ms (down from 850ms) after config change
Jamal R: Can we add a tracing gate so mutation runs as async consumer that updates storage rather than mutating outgoing spans? That keeps exporter path lean.
Tia S: Agree — decouple backfill bookkeeping from hot path. Also add a retention-overwrite test in CI that replays high-span-rate to catch perf regressions.
Maria L: Filing follow-up: reduce per-span copies, add unit test for attribute mutation cost, add long-tail perf regression to scribe. I'll make tickets. :white_check_mark:
Alex G: Thanks — I'll monitor for 24h and post results. If p99 stays <350ms we keep changes and roll to steady state.
SRE Oncall: Noted. Alerting amended to fire if exporter CPU > 70% for 10m or p99 export latency > 500ms.
Kevin P: Saved profiler and flamegraphs to /srv/debug/telemetry/1965012345-exporter-flame.svg
Alex G: Closing loop in a few hours with metrics. Good catch everyone. :pray:
